import Lean
import Obsmetrologia
open Lean Elab Command

/-!
Certificate-shape census.

The owner's charge: the library's proofs "take shortcuts and don't build up" —
tables restated as theorems, models trivialized so the theorem is free,
evocative names over finite checks. This census classifies every house
theorem by the SHAPE of its certificate, without judging truth. It is a shape
signal for human review, never a verdict: a `rfl`-headed proof over a
same-module statement can be a real one-line fact, and an `other`-headed
proof can still be a shortcut.

Per theorem (`Obsmetrologia.*`, non-internal, `.thmInfo`):

- `proofHead`: the proof term's head after stripping leading lambdas/mdata.
  `rfl` for the reflexivity family (`Eq.refl`, `rfl`, `HEq.refl`, `Iff.rfl`),
  `decide` for a `of_decide_eq_true`-headed decidability proof,
  `rfl-bundle`/`decide-bundle` for an anonymous-constructor bundle
  (`⟨rfl, rfl⟩` elaborates to `And.intro rfl rfl`, etc.) whose every
  explicit field classifies uniformly as one of those, `other` otherwise.
- `locality`: whether every house constant occurring in the theorem's TYPE
  shares the theorem's own module (the 2nd name segment after
  `Obsmetrologia.`) — `same-module` / `crosses-module` / `no-house-constants`.
- `hypothesisCount`: leading Pi binders of the type (explicit + implicit).
- `unusedHypotheses`: of those, how many go unreferenced (bvar-unused) in the
  proof value's matching leading lambdas — the vacuous-hypothesis signal
  (`hn_vanishes_above_one (_h : 2 ≤ n)` is the owner's own example).
- `propBundle`: whether the type's head constant is a house-declared
  `structure ... : Prop` (a bundle of previously proved facts).

The "self-certifying table" signal this census exists to surface is
`locality = same-module` together with `proofHead ∈
{rfl, decide, rfl-bundle, decide-bundle}` — computed by the JS aggregator
from the rows below, not printed here.

Output, tab-separated:
  `#theorems\t<n>`
  `#kinds\t<proofHead>\t<count>`   (overall tally, informational — recomputed from rows below)
  `<name>\t<module>\t<proofHead>\t<locality>\t<hypothesisCount>\t<unusedHypotheses>\t<propBundle:true|false>`
-/

def isHouse (n : Name) : Bool := n.toString.startsWith "Obsmetrologia."

/-- The string-valued dot components of a name, ignoring anonymous and numeric
segments (`Obsmetrologia.Foo.bar` -> `["Obsmetrologia", "Foo", "bar"]`). -/
partial def nameStrComponents : Name → List String
  | .anonymous => []
  | .str p s => nameStrComponents p ++ [s]
  | .num p _ => nameStrComponents p

/-- Lean-elaborator-generated declaration names -- recursors, injectivity/
no-confusion lemmas, equation-compiler helpers, sizeOf plumbing, well-founded
match/proof helpers, etc. -- that must never be counted as house theorems.
True when any dot-separated component begins with `_` (`_proof_1`, `_eq_1`,
`_unfold`, ...), or the last component is one of the fixed auto-generated
names, or begins with `match_`/`proof_`, or is `eq_` followed by one or more
digits (`eq_1`, `eq_2`, ...). A `mk.sizeOf_spec`/`mk.injEq`/`mk.inj`/
`mk.noConfusion` name is already caught by the last-component rule, since
`sizeOf_spec`/`injEq`/`inj`/`noConfusion` is its own last component. See
AGENTS.md defect note (2026-09-21): every census program in this directory
had been counting these as house theorems, inflating every "theorems" total
and (worst, in the certificate-shape census) dominating the top lists with
`Algebra.*.mk.sizeOf_spec` entries. -/
def isAutoGenerated (n : Name) : Bool :=
  let cs := nameStrComponents n
  if cs.any (·.startsWith "_") then true
  else
    match cs.getLast? with
    | none => false
    | some last =>
      [
        "sizeOf_spec", "injEq", "inj", "noConfusion", "noConfusionType",
        "casesOn", "recOn", "rec", "brecOn", "binductionOn",
        "below", "ibelow", "toCtorIdx", "ofNat_toCtorIdx", "ctorIdx", "ctorElim"
      ].contains last
      || last.startsWith "match_"
      || last.startsWith "proof_"
      || (last.startsWith "eq_" && last.length > 3 && (last.drop 3).all Char.isDigit)

/-- The second dot-separated segment of a fully-qualified Lean name — the
Obsmetrologia module a name belongs to (e.g. `Obsmetrologia.Closure.Collatz.foo`
-> `Closure`). Mirrors `moduleOf` in `src/theorem-census.mjs`. -/
def moduleOfName (n : Name) : String :=
  match n.toString.splitOn "." with
  | _ :: m :: _ => m
  | parts => String.intercalate "." parts

/-- Strip leading lambdas and mdata off a proof term to reach its
computational core (the head we classify). -/
partial def stripLambdasMdata (e : Expr) : Expr :=
  match e with
  | .lam _ _ b _ => stripLambdasMdata b
  | .mdata _ b => stripLambdasMdata b
  | _ => e

/-- The reflexivity family: any of these heading a (stripped) proof term
counts as `rfl`. -/
def rflHeadNames : List Name := [``Eq.refl, ``rfl, ``HEq.refl, ``Iff.rfl]

/-- Decidability-proof heads: what the `decide` tactic/term elaborates to. -/
def decideHeadNames : List Name := [``of_decide_eq_true]

/-- The explicit-binder-position arguments of a fully-applied constructor
application, read off the constructor's own declared type (walking its
leading `forallE` chain in lockstep with the application's argument array) —
the "field" arguments an anonymous constructor `⟨...⟩` bundles, as opposed to
its type/instance parameters. Falls back to keeping an argument past the end
of the known binder chain (should not happen for a saturated application;
conservative rather than silently dropping data). -/
def explicitArgsOf (ctorType : Expr) (args : Array Expr) : Array Expr := Id.run do
  let mut t := ctorType
  let mut result : Array Expr := #[]
  for i in [0:args.size] do
    match t with
    | .forallE _ _ b bi =>
      if bi.isExplicit then result := result.push args[i]!
      t := b
    | _ => result := result.push args[i]!
  return result

/-- Classify a proof term's computational core by its head constant. See the
module doc comment for the reading. Pragmatic and shallow by design — a
shape signal, not a verdict. -/
partial def headClass (env : Environment) (e : Expr) : String :=
  let core := stripLambdasMdata e
  match core.getAppFn with
  | .const c _ =>
    if rflHeadNames.contains c then "rfl"
    else if decideHeadNames.contains c then "decide"
    else
      match env.find? c with
      | some (.ctorInfo ctorVal) =>
        let explicitArgs := explicitArgsOf ctorVal.type core.getAppArgs
        if explicitArgs.isEmpty then "other"
        else
          let subs := explicitArgs.toList.map (headClass env)
          if subs.all (fun s => s == "rfl" || s == "rfl-bundle") then "rfl-bundle"
          else if subs.all (fun s => s == "decide" || s == "decide-bundle") then "decide-bundle"
          else "other"
      | _ => "other"
  | _ => "other"

/-- Leading Pi binders of a type (explicit and implicit alike). -/
partial def countLeadingPis (e : Expr) : Nat :=
  match e with
  | .forallE _ _ b _ => 1 + countLeadingPis b
  | _ => 0

/-- Of the first `n` leading hypotheses (as counted by `countLeadingPis` on
the type), how many go unmentioned (no loose bvar 0 in the remaining body at
the point each is peeled) in the proof value's matching leading lambdas —
the vacuous-hypothesis signal. Stops and undercounts, never guesses, if the
value runs out of leading lambdas before `n` is exhausted (an eta-reduced or
otherwise mismatched proof term). -/
partial def unusedLeadingCount (value : Expr) (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  match n, value with
  | 0, _ => 0
  | _, .mdata _ b => unusedLeadingCount b n
  | n' + 1, .lam _ _ b _ => (if b.hasLooseBVar 0 then 0 else 1) + unusedLeadingCount b n'
  | _, _ => 0

/-- The final (non-Pi) codomain of a type. -/
partial def stripLeadingForalls (e : Expr) : Expr :=
  match e with
  | .forallE _ _ b _ => stripLeadingForalls b
  | _ => e

/-- Whether `c` is a house-declared `structure ... : Prop`: a structure (in
Lean's own `isStructure` sense) whose declared codomain sort is literally
`Prop` (`Sort 0`, i.e. `.sort .zero`). -/
def isPropStructure (env : Environment) (c : Name) : Bool :=
  isHouse c && Lean.isStructure env c &&
    match env.find? c with
    | some (.inductInfo info) =>
      match stripLeadingForalls info.type with
      | .sort .zero => true
      | _ => false
    | _ => false

/-- The house modules whose constants occur in a type, deduplicated. -/
def houseModulesOfType (e : Expr) : Array String := Id.run do
  let mut mods : Array String := #[]
  for c in e.getUsedConstants do
    if isHouse c then
      let m := moduleOfName c
      if !mods.contains m then mods := mods.push m
  return mods

/-- `same-module` / `crosses-module` / `no-house-constants`, per the module
doc comment. -/
def localityOf (ownModule : String) (typeExpr : Expr) : String :=
  let mods := houseModulesOfType typeExpr
  if mods.isEmpty then "no-house-constants"
  else if mods.all (· == ownModule) then "same-module"
  else "crosses-module"

#eval show CommandElabM Unit from do
  let env ← getEnv
  let mut rows : Array String := #[]
  let mut kindCount : Std.HashMap String Nat := {}
  let mut excluded := 0
  for (n, ci) in env.constants.toList do
    if isHouse n && !n.isInternal then
      if let .thmInfo info := ci then
        if isAutoGenerated n then
          excluded := excluded + 1
        else
          let modName := moduleOfName n
          let proofHead := headClass env info.value
          let locality := localityOf modName info.type
          let hypCount := countLeadingPis info.type
          let unused := unusedLeadingCount info.value hypCount
          let bundle := match (stripLeadingForalls info.type).getAppFn with
            | .const c _ => isPropStructure env c
            | _ => false
          kindCount := kindCount.insert proofHead ((kindCount.getD proofHead 0) + 1)
          rows := rows.push s!"{n}\t{modName}\t{proofHead}\t{locality}\t{hypCount}\t{unused}\t{bundle}"
  IO.println s!"#excluded-auto-generated\t{excluded}"
  IO.println s!"#theorems\t{rows.size}"
  for (k, c) in (kindCount.toArray.qsort (fun a b => a.2 > b.2 || (a.2 == b.2 && a.1 < b.1))) do
    IO.println s!"#kinds\t{k}\t{c}"
  for r in rows.qsort (· < ·) do IO.println r
reading: This census classifies every house theorem's certificate by SHAPE, never by truth. proofHead is what heads the proof term after stripping leading lambdas/mdata: rfl (the Eq.refl/rfl/HEq.refl/Iff.rfl family), decide (an of_decide_eq_true-headed decidability proof), rfl-bundle/decide-bundle (an anonymous-constructor bundle, e.g. ⟨rfl, rfl⟩, whose every explicit field classifies uniformly as one of those), or other. locality is same-module/crosses-module/no-house-constants: whether every house constant occurring in the theorem's TYPE shares its own module. hypothesisCount/unusedHypotheses flag leading Pi binders the proof's own value never mentions (the vacuous-hypothesis signal). propBundle flags a conclusion whose head constant is a house structure ... : Prop, i.e. a bundle of previously proved facts restated as one theorem. The 'self-certifying table' signal (locality=same-module and proofHead in {rfl, decide, rfl-bundle, decide-bundle}) and the static scan's unit-type (`def X ... : Type := Unit`/`PUnit`), Prop-structure, Bool-table (`<Enum> → Bool` case tables), and rfl-theorem findings name candidates for the owner's charge that this library's proofs take shortcuts and don't build up: tables restated as theorems, models trivialized so the theorem is free, evocative names over finite checks, Unit-typed carriers standing in for cohomology, Bool tables over enumerations standing in for regime facts. EVERY NUMBER HERE IS A SHAPE SIGNAL FOR HUMAN REVIEW, NOT A VERDICT: a same-module rfl proof can be a genuine one-line fact about a real model, and an other-headed proof can still be a shortcut this census has no way to see.
